metadata.name: US GAAP (Form 10-K) line items
changes: Built by scripts/build_usgaap_pair.py: the rows the face of a Form 10-K's consolidated balance sheets, statements of operations, statements of comprehensive income and indirect-method statements of cash flows print.

The statement of comprehensive income: four sections of the statement of operations (other comprehensive income; comprehensive income attributable to; the available-for-sale securities' and the cash flow hedges' change and reclassification), scoped by the section a row is printed under. The net income it opens on is a line of its own, compared with the statement of operations' by a template identity; each block's net change, total other comprehensive income and comprehensive income are rollups.

118 statement lines, every one read from the face (strict_face_route); no internal parts. One leftover line per asset, liability, stockholders' equity and cash-flow section; none in the statement of operations, its comprehensive income or temporary equity.

Earnings per share (basic, diluted) and the weighted-average shares used to compute them (basic, diluted): four statement-of-operations lines declaring `measure: per_share` / `shares`, published as printed in dollars per share and in shares, never in the statements' scale; in no rollup and no KPI.

37 additional items, read from the notes and the auditor's report: the supplemental cash flow disclosures, debt maturities, principal and fair value, the current and deferred tax and the effective tax rate, the inventory split, property at cost and accumulated depreciation, the audit opinion, contingent liabilities and related-party transactions, with a short narrative of each of the last two written by the model and labelled as such.
metadata.vocabulary_note: English captions in the wording 10-K filers print, with the variants of the most-printed face rows.

headings: notes to the consolidated financial statements
notes to the standalone financial statements
notes forming part of the standalone financial statements
notes forming part of the consolidated financial statements
notes forming part of the financial statements

umbrella_banners.note: A 10-K balance sheet prints LIABILITIES AND STOCKHOLDERS' EQUITY above the current liabilities, the long-term liabilities and the equity; reading it as equity would refuse every liability line beneath it.
A 10-K balance sheet prints ASSETS as an umbrella over Current assets and the unheaded non-current rows. Reading it as a section of its own would scope every asset line to a section no line declares.

exclusive_vocabularies.note: ASC 230 divides cash flows into exactly three activities and a statement labels each subtotal with its own, so naming one rules out the others.

normalisation.note: Applied to every candidate row label and every alias before comparison. The quoted literals in each step are that step's own vocabulary — `row_reconstruct._quoted_examples` harvests them — so they are configuration, not illustration.
pipeline: Full-width to half-width punctuation; map ⁄ to /.
Strip footnote and note markers: trailing digits in parentheses, superscripts, '(Note 5)', '(See Note 5)', and the asterisk and dagger a 10-K hangs off a caption to key it to a footnote: '*', '†'.
Strip trailing colons and dashes used to introduce sub-captions ('Current assets:', 'Operating activities:').
Strip inline unit and currency annotations: '$', 'US$', '(in millions)', '(in thousands)', '(unaudited)'.
Collapse internal whitespace to a single space; strip zero-width characters and soft hyphens.
Join a wrapped caption to its continuation line before matching, then also retain the bare fragment as a fallback candidate.
normalisation.wrapped_caption_rule:
A 10-K equity caption is long enough to wrap: 'Common stock and additional paid-in capital, $0.00001 par value: 50,400,000 shares authorized; 15,116,786 and 15,550,061 shares issued and outstanding, respectively' is one caption on two or three physical lines, and the share counts inside it are part of the caption, not figures. Reassemble from the value row upward before matching; match the reassembled string first, and use the bare fragment only if that fails.

THE DOLLAR SIGN IS NOT A FIGURE. A 10-K prints '$' in a column of its own beside the first row of each block and beside every total; it belongs to the figure to its right. A 10-K prints no note-reference column on the face.

binding.note: Precedence is section-first. A concept can only claim a row printed inside one of its section_scope values.
order: 1. Resolve the statement (balance_sheet / profit_and_loss / cash_flow) from the page or table caption.

2. Resolve the printed section from the nearest preceding section header. If no header is resolvable, the row is unbound: route to review, never guess a section. (A row WITH a resolved section that no concept claims is not unbound — it is swept into that section's residual; see unbound_row_policy.)
3. Restrict the candidate concept set to concepts whose section_scope contains the resolved section.
4. Rule tier: exact normalised alias, then regex_hints, in descending match_priority. Any exclude_hints hit is a hard veto, not a score penalty.
5. Semantic tier over the restricted set only, using definition + include + exclude. Never over the full ontology.
6. Tie between concepts listed in each other's confusable_with: resolve with section_disambiguation; if still tied, emit both as candidates and route to review. Never pick by declaration order.
7. Residual sweep (see residual_framework) runs last, over rows no dedicated concept claimed.
8. Reconcile the section against its reported subtotal.
binding.unbound_row_policy: Route an unclaimed face value only to the residual for its resolved printed section. Never borrow a neighbouring concept or cross a section. After all mapping and gap-closing opportunities, the engine-level face_mapping_contract gives any remaining face value a unique engine_unclassified_face key outside the ontology/template namespaces. This keeps the row stored and reviewable without feeding it into an unrelated calculation. Verified non-additive aggregates replaced by mapped components remain evidence-only.
binding.match_priority: Integer 0-99, higher evaluated first. Long specific captions rank above short generic ones so 'Total assets less current liabilities' cannot be pre-empted by 'Total current liabilities' on token overlap. Residuals are 0 and unreachable by matching.

prompt: These are the consolidated financial statements of a US registrant filed on Form 10-K under US GAAP: the Consolidated Balance Sheets, the Consolidated Statements of Operations (or Income), the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income (on a page of their own or continuing the statement of operations) and the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows. Amounts are in US dollars, usually in millions or thousands except per-share amounts; the statements of operations and of cash flows print three years and the balance sheet two. Earnings per share is an amount in dollars per share and the weighted-average shares are a count of shares, each as printed and neither in the statements' millions or thousands; a bare 'Basic' or 'Diluted' row is earnings per share under an 'Earnings per share' heading and a share count under a 'Shares used in computing earnings per share' or 'Weighted-average shares outstanding' heading, and its `subheading` names the heading. The statement of comprehensive income opens on the net income: that row is the comprehensive income line's own net income, not the statement of operations' line. It prints each block of other comprehensive income — the available-for-sale securities, the cash flow hedges — as a change, a reclassification and a net change, often with the same bare captions in both blocks; the row's `subheading` names the block. Every line of the statements is a row the face of those statements prints: cite the printed statement row, never a note, and leave a line empty when the face does not print it. The additional items are read from the notes, the supplemental cash flow disclosures and the report of the independent registered public accounting firm, as each line says; a text item is copied or written exactly as its line asks, and left empty when the filing does not disclose it. A 10-K balance sheet usually prints no 'Non-current assets' or 'Non-current liabilities' heading: the rows after 'Total current assets' and before 'Total assets' are non-current assets, and the rows after 'Total current liabilities' and before the equity are non-current liabilities. Expenses are read as printed, positive.

sign_convention.stored_value: The reported value after paren-to-negative conversion.
sign_convention.expenses_and_outflows: Stored POSITIVE, as a 10-K statement of operations prints them. The template subtracts them where it computes a figure: gross profit is total revenues less cost of revenue. A cash outflow keeps the negative sign the statement of cash flows prints.
sign_convention.unsigned_source: A filing that prints expenses as unsigned positives is read as printed; nothing is negated.
sign_convention.either: Subtotals, working-capital movements, fair-value changes, share of results, OCI and net cash flows are sign-indeterminate. Retain the reported sign; never coerce.
sign_convention.validation: A concept whose sign_convention is positive_expected or negative_expected but whose loaded value carries the opposite sign is a review trigger, not an auto-correction.

global_rules.face_only_default: Concepts default to face_only: true. Notes are evidence for a face amount, never an independent source of one, unless note_use is decomposition_allowed.
global_rules.duplicate_fact_rule: The same economic fact on the face and in a note is one fact with multiple evidence references, not two additive values. This also applies to two face captions that report the same amount (see equivalence blocks).
parent_child_allocation: Never load a gross parent and its separately mapped children additively.
Residual = reported parent minus confirmed included children.
Subtract only on explicit inclusion wording, hierarchy, reconciliation or arithmetic support.
If containment is uncertain, retain the parent as evidence and route to review.
global_rules.no_fabricated_split: Never invent a decomposition. Where only a combined figure is reported, load the combined concept and leave the children empty. The one exception is a concept declaring sole_component_of: assigning a whole undifferentiated figure to a single child divides nothing, and it is refused as soon as any sibling child is evidenced on the face or in the subtotal's own note.
global_rules.totals_policy: Compute totals from mutually exclusive concept outputs. Use reported totals only for validation, never as an input to the components.

scope_selection.note: A Form 10-K presents the CONSOLIDATED financial statements of the registrant. Some also print condensed parent-company statements (Schedule I) at the back, and a few print separate statements for a subsidiary registrant; those are a second entity, not a column of the first.

entity_scope.rule: Resolve the entity from the statement's own title and column headings, never from position. A 10-K titles its statements 'Consolidated Balance Sheets', 'Consolidated Statements of Operations' (or 'of Income', 'of Earnings') and 'Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows'; condensed parent-company statements are titled 'Condensed Financial Information of Registrant' or 'Parent Company Only'. Record entity_scope on every fact and never mix the two within one statement.
company_only_markers: A balance sheet printing 'Investments in subsidiaries' (or 'Investment in consolidated subsidiaries') as an asset is a parent-company statement: consolidation eliminates it.

period_selection.rule: A 10-K's fiscal year ends on any date the registrant chooses (31 December, the last Saturday of September, 31 January). The balance sheet prints two year-end columns and the statements of operations and of cash flows print THREE fiscal years. Identify the current period from the column heading date rather than from position, load the immediately preceding year into the comparative slot, and leave the third year unread.
period_selection.restatement_rule: Where a comparative is labelled 'As Adjusted', 'Restated' or 'Recast', load it as the comparative and set restated: true. Keep both figures with the flag rather than overwriting an original comparative already loaded.

units_and_currency.rule: Resolve currency and scale from the statement header, not the cover page, and re-resolve per statement: a 10-K states its statements in millions or thousands of US dollars 'except per share amounts', and share counts are often in a different scale again. Persist unit on every fact; never normalise scale silently. A header that names two scales names the statements' first: '(In millions, except number of shares, which are reflected in thousands, and per-share amounts)' is in millions, so the '..., except' signals are declared, and matched longest first, ahead of the bare ones.
units_and_currency.conflict: If the header scale and a printed subtotal are inconsistent by a factor of 1,000, trust neither and route the statement to review: the thousands-to-millions step is the one a 10-K's statements and its notes most often differ by.

scope_selection.column_guard: Every fact carries the resolved (entity_scope, period, currency, unit). Two facts for the same canonical_key that differ on any of these are distinct facts, not duplicates — which is what keeps the standalone and the consolidated set of the same filing from colliding.

residual_framework.note: One definition governing the 11 output-template subsection residuals. Each uses an existing template line; no template row is added.

sweep.runs: after all dedicated concepts in the section have been resolved, before section reconciliation
sweep.candidate_set: every printed value row on the FACE of the statement whose resolved section equals the residual's single section_scope value
eligibility: The row printed a value for the selected entity_scope, period, currency and unit.
No dedicated concept whose section_scope contains this section claimed the row.

The row is not a section subtotal, statement total, section header, attribution caption, per-share figure, narrative row, note-reference-only row, truncated caption, an "of which" breakdown of the row above it or a sub-enumerated component of it ((a)… or 1.… beneath a numbered head) — each of those amounts is already inside the row above, so sweeping it counts the same money twice.
The row was printed INSIDE this section. A row printed in any other section is ineligible however similar its wording — there is no cross-section rescue.

The row's sign agrees with the section's sign_convention, where the section states one. A row signed against its section is evidence the SECTION is wrong, not the amount, so it goes to review rather than into the bucket — a cost swept into income moves the income subtotal and every total below it.
sweep.plug_behaviour: forbidden — the residual is never computed as (reported subtotal − mapped children)
sweep.literal_others_caption: A row captioned 'Others' or 'Miscellaneous' is simply one unmapped face row and sweeps in as a single component. It gets no privileged treatment and no dedicated concept.

itemisation.rule: The residual's value is the arithmetic sum of its components. Original labels and signs are always retained; a swept row is never relabelled to 'Others'.

reconciliation.identity: reported_section_subtotal − Σ(dedicated concepts in section) − Σ(residual components) = 0
reconciliation.tolerance: one rounding unit per contributing row
reconciliation.on_failure: Emit an unallocated_gap fact carrying the difference and route the section to review. Never adjust the residual, and never adjust a dedicated concept, to close the gap.
reconciliation.sections_without_reported_subtotal: If the section prints no subtotal, the residual is still itemised but is flagged unreconciled and carries lower confidence.

review_triggers: any single component exceeds 2% of |reported section subtotal|
a component label scored at or above the semantic threshold against a dedicated concept but was vetoed by exclude_hints
residual sign is opposite to the section's sign_convention
the section reconciliation emitted an unallocated_gap
prohibitions: Never populated by alias, regex or embedding match.
Never carries a value with no itemised components.
Never absorbs a row a dedicated concept could have claimed but was not tested for — all dedicated concepts in the section must be evaluated first.
Never spans sections, statements, periods, entity scopes or units.

items.label: Cash and cash equivalents
items.definition: Cash on hand and in banks, and short-term, highly liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less, as the balance sheet prints them. Restricted cash printed as its own row is the next line.

items.label: Restricted cash
items.definition: Cash whose use is restricted by contract or regulation, printed as its own current row.

items.label: Short-term investments
items.definition: Marketable securities and other investments held as current assets: debt and equity securities the filer expects to realise within a year.

items.label: Accounts receivable, net
items.definition: Amounts customers owe for goods and services delivered, net of the allowance for credit losses, as the balance sheet prints them. Vendor, finance and other non-trade receivables are not this line.

items.label: Inventories
items.definition: Raw materials, work in process and finished goods or merchandise held for sale, as one printed row.

items.label: Assets held for sale
items.definition: Assets of a disposal group classified as held for sale or of discontinued operations, printed as a current row.

items.label: Prepaid expenses and other current assets
items.definition: Every current-asset row the face prints that no line above claims, itemised: prepaid expenses, vendor non-trade receivables, derivative assets, income taxes receivable.
aliases: Prepaid expenses and other current assets

en: Prepaid expenses and other current assets

items.label: Total current assets
items.definition: Total current assets as printed, and the sum of the current-asset lines.

items.label: Long-term investments
items.definition: Marketable securities and other investments held beyond a year: debt securities, equity securities and non-marketable investments. Investments accounted for by the equity method are the next line.

items.label: Equity method investments
items.definition: Investments in affiliates and joint ventures the filer accounts for by the equity method (ASC 323), as one printed row.
aliases: Investments in and advances to affiliates

en: Investments in and advances to affiliates

items.label: Property, plant and equipment, net
items.definition: Land, buildings, machinery and equipment net of accumulated depreciation, as the balance sheet prints them. Assets held under finance leases printed on their own row are left to the other non-current assets.

items.label: Operating lease right-of-use assets
items.definition: The right to use leased assets under operating leases (ASC 842), as one printed row.

items.label: Goodwill
items.definition: The excess of the price paid for acquired businesses over the fair value of their net identifiable assets, as the balance sheet prints it.

items.label: Intangible assets, net
items.definition: Identifiable intangible assets other than goodwill (customer relationships, technology, trade names, licences), net of accumulated amortisation.

items.label: Deferred income tax assets
items.definition: Deferred tax assets net of any valuation allowance, printed among the assets.

items.label: Other non-current assets
items.definition: Every non-current-asset row the face prints that no line above claims, itemised: other assets, finance lease assets, long-term receivables, capitalised software, restricted cash held beyond a year.

items.label: Total non-current assets
items.definition: The sum of the non-current-asset lines. Most 10-K balance sheets print no such total; where one is printed it is read and compared.

items.label: Total assets
items.definition: Total assets as printed, and the sum of total current and total non-current assets.

items.label: Short-term debt and current portion of long-term debt
items.definition: Borrowings due within a year: commercial paper, short-term borrowings and notes payable, and the current portion of long-term debt. Where the face prints them on separate rows the rows are added, and so is the current part of finance lease obligations, which a credit analyst counts as debt. Operating lease liabilities are not this line. A bare 'Term debt' printed above the current liabilities' total is the current portion.
aliases: Long-term debt due within one year

en: Long-term debt due within one year

items.label: Accounts payable
items.definition: Amounts owed to suppliers for goods and services received, as the balance sheet prints them; where the face prints accounts payable together with accrued liabilities as one row, that row.

items.label: Accrued liabilities
items.definition: Expenses incurred and not yet paid (compensation, interest, warranties, other accruals), printed as their own rows; where the face prints several accrual rows they are added. A combined 'accrued and other current liabilities' row is the leftover line's.

items.label: Deferred revenue
items.definition: Consideration received for goods or services not yet delivered, due within a year (contract liabilities under ASC 606).

items.label: Income taxes payable
items.definition: Income taxes owed to tax authorities and due within a year, as the balance sheet prints them. Long-term income taxes payable are the other non-current liabilities.

items.label: Operating lease liabilities, current
items.definition: The part of operating lease liabilities (ASC 842) due within a year: a bare 'Operating lease liabilities' printed above the current liabilities' total.
aliases: Current portion of operating lease liabilities
Operating lease obligations due within one year

en: Current portion of operating lease liabilities
Operating lease obligations due within one year

items.label: Liabilities held for sale
items.definition: Liabilities of a disposal group classified as held for sale or of discontinued operations, printed as a current row.

items.label: Other current liabilities
items.definition: Every current-liability row the face prints that no line above claims, itemised: other current liabilities, accrued and other liabilities printed as one row, current finance lease liabilities, dividends payable.
aliases: Accrued expenses and other current liabilities

en: Accrued expenses and other current liabilities

items.label: Total current liabilities
items.definition: Total current liabilities as printed, and the sum of the current-liability lines.

items.label: Long-term debt
items.definition: Borrowings due after a year (notes, bonds, term loans), net of the current portion, as the balance sheet prints them, and the long-term part of finance lease obligations, which a credit analyst counts as debt; the rows are added. Operating lease liabilities are not this line.
aliases: Long-term debt, net of current portion
Long-term debt due after one year

en: Long-term debt, net of current portion
Long-term debt due after one year

items.label: Operating lease liabilities, non-current
items.definition: The part of operating lease liabilities (ASC 842) due after a year: a bare 'Operating lease liabilities' printed below the current liabilities' total.
aliases: Operating lease liabilities, less current portion
Operating lease liabilities, net of current portion

en: Operating lease liabilities, less current portion
Operating lease liabilities, net of current portion

items.label: Deferred income tax liabilities
items.definition: Deferred tax liabilities, printed among the liabilities; where the face prints them together with other long-term liabilities as one row, that row.

items.label: Deferred revenue, non-current
items.definition: Consideration received for goods or services to be delivered after a year.
aliases: Deferred revenue, net of current portion

en: Deferred revenue, net of current portion

items.label: Pension and postretirement benefits
items.definition: The unfunded obligation for defined-benefit pensions and other postretirement and postemployment benefits, as the balance sheet prints it.

items.label: Other non-current liabilities
items.definition: Every non-current-liability row the face prints that no line above claims, itemised: other long-term liabilities, long-term income taxes payable, finance lease liabilities, asset retirement obligations.

items.label: Total non-current liabilities
items.definition: The sum of the non-current-liability lines. Most 10-K balance sheets print no such total; where one is printed it is read and compared.

items.label: Total liabilities
items.definition: Total liabilities as printed, and the sum of total current and total non-current liabilities.

items.label: Temporary equity
items.definition: Redeemable noncontrolling interests and redeemable preferred stock printed between the liabilities and the stockholders' equity (temporary or mezzanine equity, ASC 480-10-S99). It is neither a liability nor part of total equity.

items.label: Preferred stock
items.definition: Preferred stock classified in stockholders' equity, at its carrying amount. Redeemable preferred stock is temporary equity.

items.label: Common stock
items.definition: Common stock at par or stated value, the caption usually carrying the par value and the shares authorised and issued. Where the face prints common stock and additional paid-in capital as one row, that row, and the next line is left empty.
aliases: Common stock and additional paid-in capital

en: Common stock and additional paid-in capital

items.label: Additional paid-in capital
items.definition: Amounts paid for stock above its par value, and the credit for stock-based compensation.
aliases: Capital in excess of par value

en: Capital in excess of par value

items.label: Retained earnings (accumulated deficit)
items.definition: Cumulative earnings not distributed as dividends, or the accumulated deficit.

items.label: Accumulated other comprehensive income (loss)
items.definition: The accumulated balance of other comprehensive income: currency translation, unrealised gains and losses on securities and hedges, and pension adjustments.

items.label: Treasury stock
items.definition: The cost of the filer's own shares repurchased and held in treasury, printed as a deduction.
aliases: Common stock held in treasury, at cost

en: Common stock held in treasury, at cost

items.label: Other stockholders' equity
items.definition: Every stockholders' equity row the face prints that no line above claims, itemised: deferred or unearned compensation, notes receivable from stockholders, shares held by an employee stock ownership plan, other components of the stockholders' equity. Noncontrolling interests are the next line, and redeemable interests are temporary equity, not this line.

items.label: Total stockholders' equity
items.definition: The equity of the filer's own stockholders, as printed: the sum of the equity lines above, before noncontrolling interests.

items.label: Noncontrolling interests
items.definition: The equity in consolidated subsidiaries not owned by the filer, classified in equity. Redeemable noncontrolling interests are temporary equity; a 'nonredeemable' one is this line.

items.label: Total equity
items.definition: Total equity as printed: the stockholders' equity and the noncontrolling interests.
aliases: Total stockholders' equity and noncontrolling interests

en: Total stockholders' equity and noncontrolling interests

items.label: Total liabilities and stockholders' equity
items.definition: The balance-sheet total on the right-hand side: total liabilities, temporary equity and total equity. It equals total assets.
aliases: Total liabilities, redeemable noncontrolling interest, and equity
Total liabilities, redeemable noncontrolling interest, & equity

en: Total liabilities, redeemable noncontrolling interest, and equity
Total liabilities, redeemable noncontrolling interest, & equity

items.label: Net sales
items.definition: Revenue from the sale of goods and services, where the face prints it as a row of its own above other revenue. A face printing one revenue figure prints it as total revenues.

items.label: Other revenues
items.definition: Revenue the face prints beside net sales: membership fees, franchise and licence income, other operating revenue.

items.label: Total revenues
items.definition: Total revenues as printed: the top line of the statement of operations. Where the face prints net sales and other revenues it is their sum.

items.label: Cost of revenue
items.definition: The cost of the goods and services sold, as printed, positive; where the face prints a product and a service cost and their total, the total.
aliases: Cost of goods and services sold

en: Cost of goods and services sold

items.label: Gross profit
items.definition: Total revenues less cost of revenue. Where the face prints it, that figure is read and compared.

items.label: Research and development
items.definition: Research and development expense printed as an operating expense row of its own, as printed, positive.

items.label: Selling, general and administrative
items.definition: Selling, marketing, general and administrative expense, as printed, positive. Where the face prints sales and marketing and general and administrative on separate rows, the rows are added.
aliases: Operating, selling, general and administrative expenses

en: Operating, selling, general and administrative expenses

items.label: Depreciation and amortization
items.definition: Depreciation and amortisation printed as its own operating expense row; where the face prints amortisation of intangibles separately, the rows are added. Empty where the face includes it in cost of revenue and the other expense lines.

items.label: Restructuring and impairment charges
items.definition: Restructuring, exit and impairment charges printed as operating expense rows of their own; the rows are added.

items.label: Other operating expense (income), net
items.definition: Other operating expense or income printed as a row of its own within operating expenses, with the sign the face gives it.

items.label: Total operating expenses
items.definition: Total operating expenses as printed. A multi-step statement prints it below gross profit, excluding cost of revenue; it is read as printed and not recomputed.

items.label: Total costs and expenses
items.definition: Total costs and expenses as printed. A single-step statement prints it below total revenues, including cost of revenue; it is read as printed and not recomputed.

items.label: Operating income (loss)
items.definition: Operating income or loss as printed; read as printed and not recomputed.

items.label: Interest expense
items.definition: Interest expense on debt, as printed; where the face prints interest only net of interest income, that net figure.

items.label: Interest income
items.definition: Interest and investment income on cash and securities, printed as a non-operating row of its own, with the sign the face gives it.

items.label: Other income (expense), net
items.definition: Other non-operating income and expense printed as a row of its own, with the sign the face gives it.

items.label: Total other income (expense), net
items.definition: Total non-operating income and expense as printed; read as printed and not recomputed.

items.label: Income before income taxes
items.definition: Income or loss before income taxes as printed; read as printed and not recomputed.
aliases: Income before provision for income taxes

en: Income before provision for income taxes

items.label: Provision for income taxes
items.definition: The income tax expense or benefit for the year, current and deferred together, as printed.

items.label: Equity in earnings of affiliates
items.definition: The filer's share of the earnings of equity-method investees, as printed.
aliases: Equity in net income of affiliates
Equity in earnings (losses) of unconsolidated affiliates

en: Equity in net income of affiliates
Equity in earnings (losses) of unconsolidated affiliates

items.label: Income from continuing operations
items.definition: Income or loss from continuing operations after income taxes, where the face prints it.

items.label: Income (loss) from discontinued operations
items.definition: The result of operations the filer has disposed of or classified as held for sale, net of tax, as printed below income from continuing operations.
aliases: Income (loss) from discontinued operations, net of tax

en: Income (loss) from discontinued operations, net of tax

items.label: Net income (loss)
items.definition: Net income or loss for the year as printed, including any part attributable to noncontrolling interests.
aliases: Profit of consolidated and affiliated companies

en: Profit of consolidated and affiliated companies

items.label: Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests
items.definition: The part of net income attributable to noncontrolling interests, with the sign the face gives it (often printed as a deduction).
aliases: Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests
Less: Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests
Net (income) loss attributable to noncontrolling interests
Consolidated net income attributable to noncontrolling interest
Net income attributable to noncontrolling interest

en: Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests
Less: Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests
Net (income) loss attributable to noncontrolling interests
Consolidated net income attributable to noncontrolling interest
Net income attributable to noncontrolling interest

items.label: Net income attributable to the company
items.definition: The part of net income attributable to the filer's own stockholders, where the face prints it; empty where the filer has no noncontrolling interests and prints net income alone.
aliases: Net income attributable to common stockholders
Net income attributable to the Company
Net income available to common stockholders

en: Net income attributable to common stockholders
Net income attributable to the Company
Net income available to common stockholders

items.label: Earnings per share — basic
items.definition: Basic earnings or loss per share for the year (ASC 260): net income attributable to the filer's common stockholders divided by the weighted-average common shares outstanding, in dollars per share as printed. A 10-K often prints it as a bare 'Basic' row under an 'Earnings per share' or 'Net income per share' heading; the 'Basic' printed under 'Shares used in computing earnings per share' or 'Weighted-average shares outstanding' is the share count, not this line. A single 'Basic and diluted' row is this line's. Not the per-share figure of continuing or discontinued operations alone, nor dividends declared per share. A per-share amount: it is not in the statements' millions or thousands.

items.label: Earnings per share — diluted
items.definition: Diluted earnings or loss per share for the year (ASC 260): net income attributable to the filer's common stockholders divided by the weighted-average shares outstanding together with the dilutive effect of options, restricted stock units and convertible securities, in dollars per share as printed. A 10-K often prints it as a bare 'Diluted' row under an 'Earnings per share' or 'Net income per share' heading; the 'Diluted' printed under 'Shares used in computing earnings per share' or 'Weighted-average shares outstanding' is the share count, not this line. A single 'Basic and diluted' row is the basic line's, and is not repeated here. Not the per-share figure of continuing or discontinued operations alone. A per-share amount: it is not in the statements' millions or thousands.

items.label: Weighted-average shares — basic
items.definition: The weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during the year used to compute basic earnings per share, as printed: a count of shares, in the scale the statement's header gives shares ('number of shares, which are reflected in thousands'), or the statements' own where the header excepts only per-share amounts — never an amount of money. A 10-K often prints it as a bare 'Basic' row under a 'Shares used in computing earnings per share' or 'Weighted-average shares outstanding' heading; the 'Basic' printed under 'Earnings per share' is the per-share amount, not this line. Not the shares issued or outstanding at the year-end that the balance sheet prints.

items.label: Net income (loss), as comprehensive income opens on it
items.definition: The net income or loss the statement of comprehensive income opens on, as that statement prints it: the statement of operations' net income, printed again as the first row of comprehensive income. It is this line's, never the statement of operations' net income line, so the figure is not filed twice; a template identity compares the two. Empty where the filer prints one continuous statement of operations and comprehensive income, whose net income is printed once.

items.label: Foreign currency translation adjustments
items.definition: The year's foreign currency translation adjustment recognised in other comprehensive income (ASC 830): the translation of foreign operations' net assets, with any net investment hedge and the reclassification on disposal of a foreign operation where the filer prints them inside it, net of tax as printed.

Where the filer prints the two and their total under a heading naming the securities ('Available-for-sale investments:'), this is the total — often a bare 'Net change, net of income tax ...' row whose `subheading` names the securities; the same caption under a cash-flow-hedges heading is the hedges' line. items.label: Available-for-sale debt securities: change in unrealized gains (losses)
items.definition: The change in unrealized gains and losses on available-for-sale debt securities arising in the year, before the reclassification to net income, as printed in the securities' block of other comprehensive income. A 10-K usually prints it as a bare 'Change in net unrealized gains (losses)' or 'Change in fair value' row under a heading naming the securities ('Available-for-sale investments:'), which is the row's `subheading`; the same caption under 'Cash flow hedges:' is the hedges' line, not this one. Not the block's net change.

items.label: Available-for-sale debt securities: reclassification of (gains) losses to net income
items.definition: The reclassification adjustment for (gains) losses on available-for-sale debt securities realised in the year and included in net income, with the sign the face gives it in the securities' block: printed '(gains) losses', a gain reclassified is negative and a loss positive. A 10-K usually prints it as a bare 'Less: reclassification adjustment for net (gains) losses included in net income' under the securities' heading, the row's `subheading`; the same caption under 'Cash flow hedges:' is the hedges' line.

items.label: Cash flow hedges: change in unrealized gains (losses)
items.definition: The change in unrealized gains and losses on derivatives designated as cash flow hedges arising in the year (the effective portion), before the reclassification to net income, as printed in the hedges' block of other comprehensive income. A 10-K usually prints it as a bare 'Change in net unrealized gains (losses)' or 'Change in fair value' row under a 'Cash flow hedges:' heading, which is the row's `subheading`; the same caption under an available-for-sale heading is the securities' line, not this one. Not the block's net change.

items.label: Cash flow hedges: reclassification of (gains) losses to net income
items.definition: The reclassification adjustment for (gains) losses on cash flow hedges included in net income in the year, with the sign the face gives it in the hedges' block: printed '(gains) losses', a gain reclassified is negative and a loss positive. A 10-K usually prints it as a bare 'Less: reclassification adjustment for net (gains) losses included in net income' under 'Cash flow hedges:', the row's `subheading`; the same caption under an available-for-sale heading is the securities' line.

items.label: Debt maturing in year 1
items.definition: The principal of debt due in the first fiscal year after the balance-sheet date, from the debt note's table of future principal payments or maturities: the row for that year ('2026' for a 2025 year-end). Principal, before unamortised discount and issuance costs; the current year-end only. Lease payments and interest are not this line. Cite the printed table line from the page.

items.label: Debt maturing in year 2
items.definition: The principal of debt due in the second fiscal year after the balance-sheet date, from the debt note's table of future principal payments or maturities: the row for that year ('2027' for a 2025 year-end). Principal, before unamortised discount and issuance costs; the current year-end only. Lease payments and interest are not this line. Cite the printed table line from the page.

items.label: Debt maturing in year 3
items.definition: The principal of debt due in the third fiscal year after the balance-sheet date, from the debt note's table of future principal payments or maturities: the row for that year ('2028' for a 2025 year-end). Principal, before unamortised discount and issuance costs; the current year-end only. Lease payments and interest are not this line. Cite the printed table line from the page.

items.label: Debt maturing in year 4
items.definition: The principal of debt due in the fourth fiscal year after the balance-sheet date, from the debt note's table of future principal payments or maturities: the row for that year ('2029' for a 2025 year-end). Principal, before unamortised discount and issuance costs; the current year-end only. Lease payments and interest are not this line. Cite the printed table line from the page.

items.label: Debt maturing in year 5
items.definition: The principal of debt due in the fifth fiscal year after the balance-sheet date, from the debt note's table of future principal payments or maturities: the row for that year ('2030' for a 2025 year-end). Principal, before unamortised discount and issuance costs; the current year-end only. Lease payments and interest are not this line. Cite the printed table line from the page.

items.label: Debt maturing thereafter
items.definition: The principal of debt due after the fifth fiscal year following the balance-sheet date: the 'Thereafter' row of the debt note's table of future principal payments. Lease payments and interest are not this line. Cite the printed table line from the page.

items.label: Total debt principal
items.definition: The total principal (face) amount of debt outstanding at the balance-sheet date, as the debt note prints it: the total of the table of future principal payments or the 'total principal' row, before unamortised discount, premium and issuance costs and before the current portion is deducted.

items.label: Fair value of debt
items.definition: The estimated fair value of the filer's debt at the balance-sheet date, as the debt or fair-value note states it, often in a sentence ('the fair value of our long-term debt was $88.4 billion'). Expressed in the statements' unit.

items.label: Current income tax expense
items.definition: The current part of the income tax expense for the year, federal, state and foreign together: the 'Total current' row of the income tax note's table of the components of the provision.

items.label: Deferred income tax expense (benefit)
items.definition: The deferred part of the income tax expense or benefit for the year: the 'Total deferred' row of the income tax note's table of the components of the provision. Not the deferred tax assets or liabilities at the year-end.

items.label: Effective tax rate
items.definition: The effective income tax rate for the year as the filing prints it, with its percent sign ('16.0%'): from the income tax note's rate reconciliation or the sentence stating it. The current year only.

items.label: Inventories: raw materials
items.definition: Raw materials and supplies held in inventory at the year-end, from the inventories note or the balance-sheet details note.

items.label: Inventories: work in process
items.definition: Work in process held in inventory at the year-end, from the inventories note or the balance-sheet details note.

items.label: Inventories: finished goods
items.definition: Finished goods (or finished products) held in inventory at the year-end, from the inventories note or the balance-sheet details note.

items.label: Property, plant and equipment, at cost
items.definition: Property, plant and equipment at cost, before accumulated depreciation: the gross total of the property note's table ('Gross property, plant and equipment', 'Total, at cost').

items.label: Accumulated depreciation
items.definition: Accumulated depreciation and amortisation of property, plant and equipment at the year-end, with the sign the property note gives it (usually printed as a deduction).

items.label: Independent auditor
items.definition: The registered public accounting firm that signs the report on the consolidated financial statements, as printed in its signature without the '/s/' (for example 'Hartwell & Rowe LLP'). Not the engagement partner.

items.label: Critical audit matter 1
items.definition: The title of the first critical audit matter the auditor's report communicates, copied as printed (for example 'Uncertain Tax Positions'); or the report's sentence stating that there are no critical audit matters.

items.label: Critical audit matter 2

items.label: Contingencies: the filer's assessment
items.definition: The sentence of the commitments and contingencies note (or the legal proceedings note) that states the filer's conclusion on its legal proceedings, claims and other contingencies, copied as printed: whether a loss is probable, an amount is accrued, or the outcome is not expected to have a material adverse effect (ASC 450). Empty when the notes disclose no contingencies.

items.label: Contingent liabilities: narrative
items.definition: A short narrative of the contingent liabilities the filing discloses (ASC 450 loss contingencies, ASC 460 guarantees), WRITTEN BY THE MODEL from the pages of the notes and labelled as such: every amount, date and name in it as the filing prints it.
items.prompt: In at most four sentences, describe the contingent liabilities the notes disclose — material legal proceedings, claims, regulatory, tax and environmental matters, and guarantees: what each is, whether an amount is accrued and how much, and any estimate of the reasonably possible loss. Write 'None disclosed.' when the notes disclose none.

items.label: Guarantees and letters of credit
items.definition: The guarantees, standby letters of credit and surety bonds the filer has issued and that are outstanding at the balance-sheet date, summed: the maximum potential amount of future payments the notes state (ASC 460). Not the undrawn capacity of a credit facility.

items.label: Accrued loss contingencies
items.definition: The amount recognised as a liability at the balance-sheet date for loss contingencies (litigation, claims, environmental and similar matters), as the notes state it. Empty where the filing states no amount.

items.label: Purchase obligations
items.definition: The total of the filer's unconditional purchase obligations and purchase commitments at the balance-sheet date, as the commitments note prints or states it.

items.label: Related parties: the disclosure
items.definition: The sentence of the related-party note that describes the principal related-party relationship and the transactions with it, or that states the filer had no material related-party transactions, copied as printed (ASC 850). Empty when the filing says nothing about related parties.

items.label: Related party transactions: narrative
items.definition: A short narrative of the related-party transactions the filing discloses (ASC 850), WRITTEN BY THE MODEL from the pages of the notes and labelled as such: every amount, date and name in it as the filing prints it.
items.prompt: In at most three sentences, describe the related-party transactions the notes disclose: who the related parties are by their relationship to the filer, what the transactions are, and their amounts for the year. Write 'None disclosed.' when the filing states there are none.

items.label: Sales to related parties
items.definition: Revenue from sales of goods and services to related parties during the year, as the related-party note prints or states it.

items.label: Purchases from related parties
items.definition: Purchases of goods and services from related parties during the year, including rent and fees paid to them, as the related-party note prints or states it; where the note prints several kinds on separate rows, the rows are added.

items.label: Amounts due from related parties
items.definition: Receivables from related parties at the balance-sheet date, as the related-party note prints or states them.

items.label: Amounts due to related parties
items.definition: Payables to related parties at the balance-sheet date, as the related-party note prints or states them.

others_master.note: One leftover line per asset, liability, stockholders' equity and cash-flow section: the rows of the section no line claims are swept there, itemised. The statement of operations has none, so a row no line claims is left for review.

cross_check_master.note: The calculated lines a filing prints: the printed figure is read and compared with the one the lines add up to.

prose_grammar.note: How a filing places a figure in a sentence. Authored once: measured over the 28 hand-written patterns this replaces, the subject and the connective were identical on all seven prose lines and only the destination differed.
